evidence: All three scored (weighted_mean) dimensions carry explicit independence-and-continue wording; no prompt, criterion or injected context tells the judge to stop at a failure. functional/prompt.md:13 'Once it succeeds, score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures and keep successful observations. A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row. Shared protocols reduce setup; they are not conjunctive bundles. When a setup step fails, set up the same thing again on a new job of your own...' (also line 7 'give that criterion its lowest score ... and move on'). polish/prompt.md:12 'Otherwise judge each criterion independently and continue after failures.' visual/prompt.md:12 'Otherwise grade every criterion independently with its five anchors and continue after failures.' All three also say 'Preserve every completed independent observation' for evaluator failures (functional:53, polish:18, visual:16), so a tool failure on one row is scoped to the unobserved outcome. The only zero-all clause in each scored prompt is the in-dimension global browser gate (blank/static shell or failed shared-storage check), which is the gate check 29 requires, not a stop-on-first-criterion-failure. grep for stop/halt/first fail/do not continue/remaining across all task judge.toml and prompt.md found only functional/judge.toml:326, where 'until none remain' / 'remaining count' describes message pagination, not judge control flow. Per-criterion 'Fails if any condition stated above does not hold' is intra-criterion conjunction, allowed by SKILL.md:64. Gate dimensions render and constraints use aggregation = "all_pass" and are exempt per workbook row 38. Template comparison: the template scored prompts carry equivalent wording ('Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure'); the task preserves the semantics in its own phrasing. Adversarial reasoning: (a) a broken app failing protocol S setup (e.g. job creation on J1) cannot zero the rest of functional, because the prompt directs re-setup on a new job without the broken feature and forbids sibling-verdict inheritance; (b) a conforming app is not at risk of a cascaded zero from a judge stop instruction because none exists. Remaining risk is only that a judge model may ignore instructions, which this row cannot measure and which is outside the source-wording scope; the deterministic counterpart check-batched-independence-wording.py was not executed by me (manual application only) and is owned by the deterministic reviewer.
